source_issues.evidence: before_agent_start hook only fires for cron/heartbeat sessions. Silent failure for all interactive sessions means autoRecall never injects memories into agent context for interactive use cases.

signals.topic: AG-UI protocol event streaming drops data and breaks streaming output across multiple dimensions
signals.summary: Multiple issues in the AG-UI event streaming pipeline: (1) EventEncoder._encode_sse crashes with AttributeError when handling AgentResponseUpdate (no model_dump_json method), (2) TextContent.AdditionalProperties (e.g., textContentType) are silently dropped when converting to TEXT_MESSAGE_START/TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT events, (3) MapAGUI hardcodes session=null so every request starts fresh with no conversation memory and no AuthorName mapping, (4) OTel telemetry is not emitted through AGUI even when explicitly configured. This collectively breaks rendering, session continuity, observability, and causes crashes.
signals.review_reason: High-impact cluster: count=4 with distinct but related root causes in AG-UI event streaming pipeline. Includes runtime crash (#4929, AttributeError), data loss (#4923, #4920), and critical observability gap (#4928). All four represent main-flow degradation or breakage in AG-UI which is a primary protocol for agent invocation. Count>=3 with at least two having explicit error evidence.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: AG-UI EventEncoder._encode_sse cannot handle AgentResponseUpdate
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'AgentResponseUpdate' object has no attribute 'model_dump_json'. EventEncoder._encode_sse crashes when event type is AgentResponseUpdate.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: TextContent.AdditionalProperties dropped by AsAGUIEventStreamAsync for TEXT_MESSAGE_START/TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT events
source_issues.evidence: TextContent.AdditionalProperties (e.g., textContentType: 'Markdown') is silently dropped when AsAGUIEventStreamAsync creates TextMessageStartEvent and TextMessageContentEvent. AG-UI protocol supports these extra fields via passthrough schemas but the framework does not forward them. Root cause code identified in ChatResponseUpdateAGUIExtensions.AsAGUIEventStreamAsync.

source_issues.title: AG-UI MapAGUI() doesn't use session store or map message AuthorName
source_issues.evidence: MapAGUI() hardcodes session=null when calling aiAgent.RunStreamingAsync() even when session store is configured. Every AG-UI request starts a fresh workflow with no memory. Client must round-trip entire message history each request. Source code location identified: AGUIEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs line 46.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: OTel is not emitted when invoking agent through AGUI
source_issues.evidence: When agent is invoked through AGUI (via AGUIChatClient.AsAIAgent()), no OTel telemetry is emitted despite explicit tracer provider configuration with AddSource for Microsoft.Extensions.Agents. Calling the same agent directly (not via AGUI) produces expected telemetry. Screenshots provided showing telemetry missing via AGUI path.

signals.topic: MCP tool integration fails in Python: hang on resource notifications and YAML binding not supported
signals.summary: Two distinct MCP tool integration failures in Python: (1) MCPStdioTool.call_tool hangs indefinitely when the MCP server sends resource/updated notifications during tool execution, even though the underlying mcp SDK handles it correctly. No timeout or cancellation recovery. (2) MCP tool binding by reference in declarative YAML is not recognized; _parse_tool in AgentFactory ignores the bindings field for MCP tools, resulting in empty server_url and 500 errors.
aliases: MCP tool binding YAML not supported
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but both MCP-related failures with clear user impact: (1) #4896 causes indefinite hang blocking tool calls, with direct comparison proving the underlying SDK works — the framework layer is the culprit; (2) #4927 causes HTTP 500 errors and forces users to couple sensitive infrastructure config into every workflow YAML. Both have explicit error evidence.

source_issues.title: Python: MCPStdioTool.call_tool hangs when MCP server sends resource notifications during tool execution
source_issues.evidence: call_tool hangs indefinitely. Logs show: 'INFO:agent_framework._mcp:[resources]: Resource updated: debug://mongodb' then hangs. Underlying mcp SDK ClientSession.call_tool completes correctly with same server. No timeout or recovery mechanism. request_timeout parameter is ignored during the hang. Verified with mongodb-mcp-server@1.9.0, Python 3.14, agent-framework-core 1.0.0rc5.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Support MCP tool binding by reference in declarative YAML
source_issues.evidence: When MCP tool is passed via bindings to AgentFactory with declarative YAML, _parse_tool ignores the bindings field for MCP case. Results in server_url: '' being sent to API, returning HTTP 500. FunctionTool correctly resolves bindings but MCP path does not. Two related problems: no HTTP header support in YAML schema and no way to reference MCP connection by identifier.

signals.topic: ChatClientAgent throws when combining ChatHistoryProvider with Azure OpenAI Responses API in stateless mode
signals.summary: ChatClientAgent throws 'Only ConversationId or ChatHistoryProvider may be used' exception when using ChatHistoryProvider with Azure OpenAI Responses API even when the request is explicitly stateless (store=false). The ConversationId is incorrectly surfaced from the adapter chain even though the HTTP response has no conversation field. This blocks users from using client-side history management with Azure OpenAI Responses.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker: ChatClientAgent crashes (NotSupportedException) when using the documented ChatHistoryProvider pattern with Azure OpenAI Responses API, even when explicitly configuring stateless mode. Users cannot use client-side history management with this API combination, which is a primary use case. Explicit HTTP evidence and full stack trace provided.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: ChatClientAgent throws when using ChatHistoryProvider with Azure OpenAI Responses API and store=false
source_issues.evidence: Exception thrown: 'Only ConversationId or ChatHistoryProvider may be used, but not both. The service returned a conversation id indicating server-side chat history management, but the agent has a ChatHistoryProvider configured.' Full stack trace provided. HTTP traffic captured showing store=false in request and no conversation field in response. Root cause: UpdateSessionConversationId throws when both ConversationId and ChatHistoryProvider are present.

signals.topic: CompactionProvider causes chat history duplication in InMemoryChatHistoryProvider across session round-trips
signals.summary: CompactionProvider re-adds previously persisted user messages into InMemoryChatHistoryProvider after session serialization and reload, even when summarization is configured to never trigger (TokensExceed int.MaxValue). Results in duplicated history entries on every multi-turn session. Data integrity issue in a core agent pattern.
signals.review_reason: Chat history data integrity issue: CompactionProvider causes message duplication in InMemoryChatHistoryProvider on session round-trips, even when summarization is disabled. Complete repro test case provided with explicit assertion showing duplicate entries. Affects session-based multi-turn conversations which is a primary use case.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: CompactionProvider re-adds previously persisted request messages to InMemoryChatHistoryProvider across session round-trips, even when summarization never triggers
source_issues.evidence: Full repro test case provided (Moq-based). After two session round-trips with JSON serialization in between, messages array contains duplicates: [hello, assistant hello, hello (dup), user who are you, assistant I am]. Root cause suspected: interaction between CompactionProvider state restoration and ChatHistoryPersistingChatClient persistence markers. Issue reproduces even when compaction is configured to never trigger.

signals.topic: Tool response serialization failure prevents LLM from using tool call results for conditional branching (Python/.NET)
signals.summary: LLM calls a tool that returns a boolean result (true/false), but the result is not correctly serialized/processed, preventing the LLM from using the tool result to make decisions. Specifically, when Function A returns true, Function B is not triggered even though the condition is satisfied. The LLM appears unable to use the runtime result of Function A to conditionally trigger sub-agent tool invocation.
aliases: Tool return value not used by LLM
Tool result serialization LLM decision making
signals.review_reason: Tool result serialization failure breaks a core agentic pattern (conditional tool chaining based on tool return values). When the LLM calls a tool that returns a boolean result to drive branching logic, the decision is not made correctly. Screenshots from production scenario provided. Affects both Python and .NET. Labeled 'need info' suggesting incomplete diagnosis but evidence of user-visible failure is clear.

source_issues.title: Python: .NET:Python: [Bug]: Tool response serialization failure.
source_issues.evidence: ICM-carried issue. LLM calls Function A which returns boolean true/false. Function B should be conditionally invoked based on Function A's result but is not triggered. Screenshots show LLM unable to use Function A runtime result to decide whether to invoke sub-agent tool. Flow: tool call → return value → conditional decision broken.

signals.topic: Tool call ID string length exceeds OpenAI's 40-character limit causing workflow-blocking BadRequestError
signals.summary: AutoGen generates tool call IDs (e.g., UUID-based) that exceed OpenAI's 40-character maximum length limit, causing BadRequestError 400 on every tool call in GroupChat/multi-agent workflows. The entire agent workflow is blocked with no fallback or recovery.
aliases: tool_calls id string length exceeds limit
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking bug: AutoGen generates tool call IDs that exceed OpenAI's 40-character limit, causing BadRequestError 400 on every tool call. The user's entire multi-agent GroupChat workflow crashes with RuntimeError. This is a clear, reproducible main-flow failure with a full stack trace showing the exact UUID-based ID that is too long.

source_issues.title: Tool id string too long
source_issues.evidence: User reports openai.BadRequestError: 'Invalid messages[3].tool_calls[0].id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 40, but got a string with length 41 instead.' The tool id `python_analyst_5694c56d-6c52-4f8b-8da4-7e5b331e2210/5694c56d-6c52-4f8b-8da4-7e5b331e2210` has length 41, exceeding the 40-char limit. Workflow crashes at GroupChat execution with RuntimeError wrapping BadRequestError, completely blocking the multi-agent task.

signals.topic: response.body() returns mojibake (double-encoded UTF-8) for SSE streaming responses in Chromium
signals.summary: When reading SSE (Server-Sent Events) streaming responses via response.body(), Playwright returns double-encoded UTF-8 (mojibake) instead of correct raw bytes. This makes Chinese/Japanese/Unicode text unreadable and breaks SSE-based streaming integrations. Affects Chromium (marked upstream). Same reporter confirmed in playwright-python and playwright-dotnet as well.
signals.review_reason: P0: count=2 (2 repos), user-impact confirmed via detailed byte-level repro. SSE streaming is a core integration pattern. Unicode text corruption makes entire feature class unusable. Labelled upstream Chromium, but still blocks Playwright users on Chromium.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: response.body() returns mojibake (double-encoded UTF-8) for SSE streaming responses
source_issues.evidence: Chromium-only bug. response.body() returns mojibake bytes (e.g. 'ä½ å¥½' instead of '你好') while route.fetch() returns correct bytes. Provides full repro with Node.js SSE server/client. CDP Network.getResponseBody() also shows corrupted bytes, indicating upstream Chromium issue. Reporter confirmed same bug in playwright-python and playwright-dotnet.

source_issues.title: response.body() returns mojibake (double-encoded UTF-8) for SSE streaming responses
source_issues.evidence: Same reporter confirms same bug in playwright core. References playwright-python issue #3023. Shows raw bytes comparison proving mojibake output (double-encoded UTF-8 byte sequences like 0xc3 0xa4 instead of correct 0xe4).

signals.topic: --last-failed silently drops all tests when using project dependencies
signals.summary: Running `playwright test --last-failed` with project dependencies configured results in 'No tests found' error, silently dropping all tests. The postShardTestFilters (used by --last-failed) runs before dependency projects are added to rootSuite, causing all dependency tests to be filtered out. Breaks the core CI/CD re-run-failed workflow.
aliases: last-failed No tests found with dependencies
signals.review_reason: P0: Main test runner workflow completely broken for any project using dependencies. Silent failure (no tests found) means entire test re-run is lost. Root cause pinpointed with instrumentation proof. Affects v1.60 label (upcoming release), blocking users adopting the feature.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: --last-failed silently drops all tests when using project dependencies
source_issues.evidence: Full root cause analysis provided: postShardTestFilters runs on line 173-174 before dependency projects are added on lines 179-180 in runner/loadUtils.js. Provides instrumentation proof showing failed test IDs from 'default' project never match 'sequential' tests. Reproducible 100%. Critical CI/CD blocker — users cannot re-run only failed tests from dependency project setups.

signals.topic: ffmpeg child process orphaned when no frames are recorded, causing Node process hang
signals.summary: In Playwright 1.58.2, when video recording is started but no frames are captured (e.g. page loads without visible changes), the ffmpeg child process is not properly terminated. This causes the Node.js process to hang indefinitely waiting for the orphaned ffmpeg stdin. Actively affecting production systems (Cloudflare telescope). Fixed in main branch but not yet released.
signals.review_reason: P1: Process hang is a resource leak that blocks CI runners and local dev. Affects production (Cloudflare telescope). Fix exists in main but users on stable 1.58.2 remain exposed. Count=1 so P0 threshold not met, but high user impact warrants P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ffmpeg orphaned if no frames are recorded
source_issues.evidence: Node process hangs indefinitely because ffmpeg child process is lost and waiting for stdin. Reproducible via external repro repo. Actively causing production hangs in Cloudflare telescope. Fix committed to main (commit d039c403) but not yet released. Affects stable 1.58.2.

signals.topic: Trace viewer fails to open large traces (>10MB) in embedded/service worker context
signals.summary: Playwright trace viewer (both local show-trace and trace.playwright.dev) fails to open traces from complex/long-running tests. Large uncompressed .trace/.network files inside the zip cause TextWriter/BlobWriter to call Response.blob() from a ReadableStream in Chromium's Service Worker, which throws 'TypeError: Failed to fetch' above ~10MB. Cascading errors in zip.js also crash the stream pipeline.
aliases: trace viewer TypeError Failed to fetch
Service Worker blob() large trace failure
signals.review_reason: P1: Trace viewer is a core debugging tool. Failing to open traces from complex tests (the ones most likely to need debugging) is a significant workflow blocker. Count=1 so P0 threshold not met, but full technical analysis and proposed fix indicate high confidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Trace viewer fails to open trace: Could not load trace from
source_issues.evidence: Full technical analysis with three root causes in ZipTraceLoaderBackend. Provides proposed fix using Uint8ArrayWriter instead of TextWriter/BlobWriter. Fails reproducibly on traces >10MB. Both trace.playwright.dev and local show-trace affected. Critical for debugging complex E2E tests.

signals.topic: Embedded trace viewer in VS Code extension shows nothing with Playwright 1.58.0 (regression from 1.57.0)
signals.summary: After upgrading from Playwright 1.57.0 to 1.58.0, the trace viewer embedded in the Playwright Test for VS Code extension renders completely empty, even though standalone show-trace works correctly and trace.zip files are valid. Downgrading to 1.57.0 restores functionality. Breaks the in-IDE debugging experience.
aliases: VS Code extension trace viewer regression 1.58
signals.review_reason: P1: Confirmed regression between 1.57 and 1.58.0, not fixed in subsequent 1.58.x. Inline debugging is a primary workflow for Playwright users; empty trace viewer defeats the purpose. Count=1 but explicit version comparison and downgrade confirmation make this high-confidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Embedded trace viewer in VS Code extension shows nothing with Playwright 1.58.0 (works with 1.57.0)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression: downgrading to 1.57.0 fixes the issue completely. Traces are valid (standalone show-trace works). Both extension versions 1.1.15 and 1.1.17 affected. Reproducible on macOS with Cursor IDE.

signals.topic: TextChunker splits oversized chunks causing silent data loss in embedding/reranking pipelines
signals.summary: TextChunker.SplitPlainTextParagraphs uses word-count instead of token-count when gluing orphan chunks, causing the last chunk to exceed the target max tokens. This results in oversized chunks that are silently dropped during embedding generation or reranking.
aliases: TextChunker word count vs token count
signals.review_reason: Confirmed code defect causes oversized chunks that silently exceed the configured max token limit. Users of embedding pipelines or rerankers built on SemanticKernel will silently lose data at the chunk level without any error being raised. This is a data-integrity defect in a core utility class used across RAG workflows.

source_issues.title: Bug: the TextChunker.SplitPlainTextParagraphs sometimes overcount the chunk sizes
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed code defect: ProcessParagraphs orphan chunk gluing logic uses number of words instead of tokens (TextChunker.cs L195-L201). Frequently silent data loss when generating embeddings or using reranker. Labeled as bug.

signals.topic: Google AI connector leaks model internal thinking/reasoning text into application-visible ChatMessageContent
signals.summary: When Gemini thinking mode is enabled (include_thoughts: true), the GoogleAIChatCompletion connector fails to filter out thought=True text parts. The model's internal reasoning (e.g. '**Processing the Task Request** Okay, the task creation was successful...') is surfaced as the application response instead of the actual answer.
aliases: GoogleAI thought text exposed to app
signals.review_reason: When Gemini thinking mode is active, the connector returns the model's internal monologue as the user-facing response. Applications consuming ChatMessageContent receive garbage (internal reasoning text) instead of the actual answer, corrupting the primary output of the AI interaction. This is a direct data-integrity failure in a production connector.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Google AI connector leaks thinking/thought text parts into ChatMessageContent
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed in semantic-kernel==1.41.1: with gemini-3-pro-preview and thinking_config include_thoughts=true, model reasoning text appears as the final ChatMessageContent instead of the actual answer. The _create_chat_message_content and _create_streaming_chat_message_content methods add all text parts without checking part.thought. Reproduction steps provided; companion PR #13711 filed.

signals.topic: Npgsql 10.x upgrade breaks Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.PgVector at runtime
signals.summary: Upgrading Npgsql to version 10.0.2 (a common scenario when combining Entity Framework Core with PgVector) causes a MissingMethodException at runtime. The PgVector connector calls NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypesAsync() which was removed or changed in Npgsql 10, crashing during CollectionExistsAsync().
signals.review_reason: Upgrading Npgsql to 10.x — a routine dependency update — causes the PgVector connector to crash entirely with MissingMethodException. This blocks the entire semantic search pipeline (CollectionExistsAsync) and is triggered by a realistic production scenario (EF Core + PgVector sharing Npgsql). The crash is immediate and unrecoverable without downgrading Npgsql.

source_issues.title: Bug: System.MissingMethodException: 'Method not found: 'System.Threading.Tasks.Task Npgsql.NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypesAsync()''.
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed MissingMethodException at runtime when Npgsql 10.0.2 is used with Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.PgVector. CollectionExistsAsync() crashes because NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypesAsync() no longer exists in Npgsql 10. Triggers when combining EF Core with PgVector (a realistic production setup). Reproduction steps provided with labeled bug tag.

signals.topic: Thinking/extended reasoning feature not functional with AWS BedrockChatClient
signals.summary: Users cannot enable the thinking (extended reasoning) feature when using BedrockChatClient with ChatClientAgent. The configuration fails validation with a required field error related to thinking.signature, making the thinking feature inaccessible on AWS Bedrock.
signals.review_reason: Extended reasoning (thinking mode) is a key feature for improving LLM output quality, but it is completely non-functional for AWS Bedrock users. This blocks an entire class of users from using a featured capability that works in other connectors, making it a key-function unavailable scenario.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Cannot enable thinking for BedrockChatClient with ChatClientAgent
source_issues.evidence: Cannot enable thinking feature for BedrockChatClient — validation error about thinking.signature field being required. Labeled as bug with .NET and triage tags. Full code sample and stack trace provided.

signals.topic: MCP plugins silently ignored when KernelArguments are provided to ChatCompletionAgent
signals.summary: Passing KernelArguments to ChatCompletionAgent (e.g., for enforcing a Pydantic response schema) causes all registered MCP plugins to be completely ignored. No function calls are emitted to MCP servers. The bug is silent — no error or warning is raised.
aliases: MCP plugins not called with KernelArguments
MCP function calls missing when schema enforced
signals.review_reason: When users pass KernelArguments (a common pattern for structured output or parameter injection), all MCP plugins are silently disabled. Applications may not detect this and will proceed without tool calls, leading to degraded or incorrect AI behavior with no indication of the failure. This is a silent but complete breakage of MCP integration in a common usage pattern.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: MCP Plugins are ignored when KernelArguments are provided to a ChatCompletionAgent
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed silent failure: when ChatCompletionAgent is instantiated with KernelArguments (e.g. for Pydantic schema enforcement), MCP plugins emit zero function calls. Removing the arguments parameter restores MCP functionality. No error or warning raised — plugins silently do nothing. Labeled as bug.

signals.topic: Mac 端 Automations 因沙箱限制全面失败，且错误历史被隐藏导致无法诊断
signals.summary: Mac 用户的所有 automations 在新版沙箱限制后无法访问网络而全面失败，且 app 立即将失败的 automation 归档，用户无法查看失败历史和原因，只能眼睁睁看着核心功能完全不可用，导致订阅用户直接退订。
aliases: Mac automation network access blocked by sandbox
signals.review_reason: 两条 issue 均为同一 Mac 用户在同一时间段提交，内容高度重叠，均指向 Mac 沙箱策略变更后 automations 无法联网且失败历史被归档隐藏。这是主流程阻断（automations 是付费核心功能）+ 体验严重下降（用户完全无法诊断）+ 直接导致退订的高影响问题，符合 P0 标准。

source_issues.title: Automations fail

source_issues.title: Automations fail, archive themselves - totally useless

signals.topic: 周限额续期后以异常速度消耗，疑似订阅状态错误导致降级计费

signals.topic: Approval remember 功能失效，每次操作都强制重新审批，严重破坏工作流效率

source_issues.title: Approvals not working

Windows TTY detection broken for resume

Model calls non-existent tool causing task failure

signals.topic: Prompt caching drops to 0% when using base64 file inputs, causing significant cost increase
signals.summary: When mixing text-only and base64 file-input requests in Agents SDK, prompt cache hit rate drops to 0% on the first file-input round even when the static prefix, tool definitions, and system instructions remain unchanged. Subsequent repeated file inputs recover to ~90%. This causes direct API cost loss for every new file input request that should have shared the cached prefix.
aliases: prompt cache hit rate zero base64 file input
cache efficiency loss with file inputs
signals.review_reason: User reports measurable cache hit rate collapse (96.7% → 0%) on the first file-input request, directly causing increased API token costs. The issue is reproducible across multiple rounds and confirmed against both Agents SDK and Responses API directly. Not a feature request — this is a regression or design flaw in how file inputs interact with prompt caching prefix matching.

source_issues.title: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64 file inputs
source_issues.evidence: User reports consistent cache_hit=0.0% when introducing file inputs via base64, compared to 96.7% for text-only rounds. Even though the static prefix, tool definitions, and system instructions are unchanged. This causes direct cost increase for repeated text+file workflows.

signals.topic: griffe dependency version conflict causes ImportError crash in CI and services
signals.summary: When both griffe 1.15.0 and griffelib 2.0.0 are installed (e.g., via uv pip), they overwrite each other, causing an ImportError at module load time: 'cannot import name ExprInterpolation from griffe._internal.expressions'. This crashes the entire agents library at import, blocking CI pipelines and production services.
signals.review_reason: ImportError at module load time causes full application crash — no agent can run until this is resolved. The user explicitly reports CI and service crashes, making this a startup-blocking issue with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: maybe use griffelib instead of griffe as dependency, and update to 2+
source_issues.evidence: User reports CI and service crashes with ImportError: 'cannot import name ExprInterpolation from griffe._internal.expressions'. Crash occurs at module import time in agents/tool.py. Root cause is a known version conflict between griffe and griffelib when both are present in the environment.

signals.topic: LitellmModel sends OpenAI-style dict reasoning_effort to non-OpenAI providers causing silent parameter mismatch
signals.summary: LitellmModel constructs dict-valued {"effort": "low", "summary": "auto"} for reasoning_effort whenever model_settings.reasoning.summary is set, but LiteLLM's Anthropic transformer only handles string-valued reasoning_effort. This causes the summary parameter to be silently ignored for all non-OpenAI providers routed through LitellmModel, resulting in unexpected model behavior without any error or warning.
aliases: reasoning summary silently ignored via LiteLLM non-OpenAI providers
reasoning_effort dict shape not portable across LiteLLM providers
signals.review_reason: Reasoning configuration (summary) is silently ignored for all non-OpenAI providers via LitellmModel, with no error or warning. This causes unexpected model behavior in production — users believe their reasoning settings are active when they are not. The issue is fully traced to the SDK code path and confirmed against LiteLLM's transformer logic.

source_issues.title: LitellmModel sends dict-valued reasoning_effort to non-OpenAI providers when reasoning.summary is set
source_issues.evidence: User traces code path showing LitellmModel constructs dict-valued reasoning_effort and LiteLLM's Anthropic transformer only maps it when it's a string, causing reasoning.summary to be silently dropped for all non-OpenAI providers. No error or warning is raised, so users are unaware their reasoning configuration is not being applied.

signals.topic: ToolCallItem.to_input_item() drops title and description during session persistence round-trip
signals.summary: ToolCallItem.title (added in #2621) and ToolCallItem.description (added in #2381) are present in-memory but are dropped when persisting session state via save_result_to_session → run_item_to_input_item → to_input_item(). The base RunItemBase.to_input_item() uses model_dump(exclude_unset=True) which excludes these SDK-local fields. This causes data loss for any workflow using session persistence with tool calls that carry title/description metadata.
aliases: tool call metadata lost on session save
signals.review_reason: Data loss bug: ToolCallItem.title and description are silently dropped during session persistence, breaking any workflow that relies on tool call metadata being preserved across save/restore cycles. The user provides a clear minimal repro demonstrating the bug. This is a regression introduced by recent feature additions (#2621, #2381) that were not wired up to the persistence path.

source_issues.title: ToolCallItem.to_input_item() drops title and description on session persistence
source_issues.evidence: User provides a minimal repro showing that to_input_item() returns a dict without 'title' or 'description' keys even though the ToolCallItem was constructed with those fields. Root cause is model_dump(exclude_unset=True) in the base class not including SDK-local fields. This breaks any session persistence workflow relying on tool call metadata.

signals.topic: Responses API: 未文档化的 reasoning+message 配对约束导致多轮对话静默产生孤立项，后续轮次 400
signals.summary: reasoning+message 必须在 input 中连续成对出现，但 SDK 文档未说明此约束。用户在第二轮对话前过滤 response.output 时会静默产生孤立 reasoning 项，导致 400 错误。
signals.review_reason: 高频（2条issue）+ 主流程阻断（Responses API 多轮对话完全不可用）+ 有生产案例（OpenClaw 64.9k forks 全部受影响）。两个 issue #3009 和 #3008 根因互补：前者是文档缺失导致用户错误过滤，后者是序列化产生 null 导致 API 拒绝，共同导致多轮对话失效。

source_issues.title: Responses API: undocumented reasoning+message pairing constraint breaks multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: reasoning+message items must appear as consecutive pairs in input. Filtering response.output to keep only messages silently produces orphaned items → 400 on next turn. This broke OpenClaw (64.9k forks) on gpt-5.3-codex.

source_issues.title: Responses API: multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
source_issues.evidence: Separate but related: model_dump() additionally generates null fields the API rejects. Both issues prevent multi-turn from working.

signals.topic: Responses API: model_dump() 序列化的 null 字段导致 API 返回 400 阻断多轮对话
signals.summary: SDK 序列化 response.output 回传为 input 时，model_dump() 会为从未返回的字段生成 null 值（如 status: null），API 拒绝未知参数为 null 的请求，导致多轮对话在第二轮必定 400 失败。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：多轮对话是 Responses API 的核心场景，第二轮必现 400 错误，完全无法使用。issue #3009 和 #3008 同属 Responses API 多轮对话根因，前者聚焦文档缺失，后者明确指出 model_dump() 序列化行为是技术根因。

source_issues.title: Responses API: multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
source_issues.evidence: model_dump() fabricates status: None, encrypted_content: None for fields the API never returned. API rejects null unknown parameters with 400: Unknown parameter: 'input[1].status'. This is a hard blocker for any multi-turn conversation using response.output as next-turn input.

signals.topic: prompt_cache_retention 参数类型声明使用连字符 'in-memory' 但 API 实际要求下划线 'in_memory'，使用时必定 400
signals.summary: SDK 在 Responses API 和 Chat Completions API 的 prompt_cache_retention 参数中声明了 Literal['in-memory', '24h']（连字符），但 API 只接受 'in_memory'（下划线），用户直接使用 SDK 类型声明的值会 100% 失败。
signals.review_reason: 类型声明与 API 实际行为不匹配，用户无论是否看文档，只要使用 SDK 类型声明的值就必然触发 400，导致 prompt caching 功能完全无法使用。issue 提供了完整的 PoC 脚本证明两边值的不一致。

source_issues.title: `prompt_cache_retention` type declares `"in-memory"` but API expects `"in_memory"`
source_issues.evidence: SDK declares Literal['in-memory', '24h'] (hyphen) but API rejects 'in-memory' with 400 and only accepts 'in_memory' (underscore). Using the SDK-typed value always fails. Includes PoC script proving both directions.

signals.topic: AsyncStream 缺少 aclose() 方法导致使用 instrumentation 库（Langfuse）时出现 AttributeError
signals.summary: AsyncStream 类只有 close() 没有 aclose()，但 Python async 规范要求使用 aclose()。当 Langfuse 等 instrumentation 库包装流对象时，__aexit__ 链调用 aclose() 会触发 AttributeError，阻断 structured output 流的正常使用。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：使用 structured output + streaming + Langfuse 等常见 instrumentation 组合时，__aexit__ 必然触发 AttributeError。Langfuse 在 AI 开发生态中使用广泛，此问题影响所有在该组合下使用 async streaming 的用户。

source_issues.title: AsyncStream missing aclose() causes AttributeError in streaming structured output
source_issues.evidence: AsyncStream has close() but not aclose(). When Langfuse wraps the stream, __aexit__ chain calls aclose() on the AsyncStream → AttributeError. Full traceback provided. Also linked to langfuse/langfuse#5685 as root cause.

signals.topic: openai-python v2.24.0 开启 DEBUG 日志时 model_dump() 的 by_alias=None 导致 pydantic-core TypeError 崩溃
signals.summary: v2.24.0 中 _compat.py 的 model_dump() 将 by_alias=None 直接传给 pydantic v2 的 Rust 序列化器，pydantic-core 不接受 None 值。DEBUG 日志路径触发该调用，导致任何 API 调用在发送前崩溃。
signals.review_reason: 版本退化（regression）：v2.24.0 引入的崩溃，任何用户在开启 DEBUG 日志后使用 SDK（包括 AzureOpenAI）进行任何 API 调用都会在网络请求发出前崩溃。影响面覆盖所有使用该版本的 DEBUG 日志用户。

source_issues.title: Bug: `by_alias: NoneType` in openai-python v2.24.0 when logging.DEBUG is enabled
source_issues.evidence: model_dump() passes by_alias=None to pydantic's model_dump(). pydantic-core v2 Rust serializer raises: TypeError: argument 'by_alias': 'NoneType' object cannot be converted to 'PyBool'. Triggered by any API call when openai logger has DEBUG level enabled. Complete reproduction script provided.

signals.topic: Discord gateway crashes with maxAttempts=0 on WebSocket disconnect, killing the process
signals.summary: Discord WebSocket reconnect handler resolves maxAttempts to 0 instead of the expected default value, causing an uncaught exception that permanently kills the Discord lifecycle on the first abnormal close (code 1006). The gateway process survives but Discord is dead, requiring manual restart.
aliases: Discord WebSocket crash max reconnect attempts
signals.review_reason: Discord integration becomes completely non-functional on first WebSocket disconnect — process-killing crash, no reconnect. User must manually restart gateway. Two independent reports (#55367, #55350) confirm the same root cause. Main Discord flow is blocked.

source_issues.title: Discord gateway crash: maxAttempts resolves to 0, uncaught exception kills process
source_issues.evidence: Uncaught exception Error: Max reconnect attempts (0) reached after code 1005/1006 — process.kill of entire OpenClaw gateway; no reconnect attempted. Discord is completely dead after first disconnect.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Discord gateway crashes with "Max reconnect attempts (0)" on WebSocket close code 1006
source_issues.evidence: Discord WebSocket drops with code 1006 (abnormal closure); reconnect handler reports maxAttempts=0 and permanently kills Discord lifecycle via shouldStopLifecycle:true. Full restart required.

signals.topic: Slack DM inbound messages silently truncated at exactly 160 characters
signals.summary: Slack DM messages exceeding 160 characters are silently truncated with no error, and the agent processes the truncated message as if complete. Users lose message content without any indication.
signals.review_reason: Slack DM messages are silently truncated at 160 chars with no error logged. Users lose message content mid-thought and receive incorrect agent responses — this is a silent data loss issue affecting the main Slack messaging flow. Reproducible deterministically at the 160-char boundary.

source_issues.title: Slack DM inbound messages truncated at exactly 160 characters (human → bot)
source_issues.evidence: Messages over 160 chars are silently cut at exactly char 160. No error is logged. Agent processes truncated message as complete, leading to incorrect/incomplete responses.

signals.topic: WhatsApp message send treats MP3 files as voice/PTT notes, breaking Android playback
signals.summary: Using openclaw message send --media with an MP3 file sends it as a WhatsApp voice/PTT note instead of a normal audio file or document. Android recipients receive an unplayable audio message, while iPhone/WhatsApp Web work fine.
signals.review_reason: Outbound WhatsApp file sending produces unplayable audio for Android recipients (large user base). MP3 files are sent as PTT voice notes which Android cannot decode. Clear file format mismatch in the message send media path.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp message send sends MP3 audio as PTT voice note, breaking Android playback
source_issues.evidence: openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --media <file.mp3> sends as PTT/voice note. Android recipients see 'This audio is not available' — file is unplayable. Affects any MP3 file sent via WhatsApp outbound path.

signals.topic: WhatsApp message send --force-document flag is silently ignored in the gateway payload
signals.summary: The --force-document CLI flag for WhatsApp message send is accepted but does not make it into the outbound gateway payload. Files are still sent via the media/audio path regardless of the flag, making the option non-functional.
signals.review_reason: A documented CLI flag (--force-document) is silently dropped before reaching the gateway payload. Users who explicitly request document delivery cannot achieve it via the CLI. Clear gap between CLI layer and transport layer.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp message send drops --force-document before gateway payload
source_issues.evidence: --force-document flag is accepted by CLI but does not appear in gateway payload. The media/file is sent via audio/media path regardless. Gap between CLI layer and gateway transport layer.

signals.topic: Global skills incorrectly take precedence over workspace-level skills in loading order
signals.summary: OpenClaw documentation states workspace skills should take precedence over global skills, but the actual behavior loads global (root-level) skills first when both have the same name. This contradicts documented precedence.
signals.review_reason: Skill loading order contradicts documented behavior — global skills run instead of workspace skills when names conflict. Users relying on workspace-level overrides get wrong skill execution. Confirmed reproducible with clear steps.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Global Skills take precedence over workspace skills in loading
source_issues.evidence: When two skills share the same name (one at root level, one at workspace level), OpenClaw loads the root/global skill instead of the workspace-level skill. Contradicts documented loading precedence. Steps to reproduce provided.

signals.topic: Uncaught PermissionError on startup preventing app launch
signals.summary: Aider crashes immediately on launch when it cannot write to ~/.aider/caches/versioncheck due to insufficient file permissions, preventing the entire application from starting.
aliases: Permission denied on cache file creation
signals.review_reason: This is a complete application startup crash with a clear traceback. The app exits immediately with an uncaught PermissionError in versioncheck.py line 95's .touch() call. The main() function never reaches the interactive loop, making the tool entirely unusable for affected users. Users running as non-root or in restricted container environments are directly impacted.

source_issues.title: Uncaught PermissionError in pathlib.py line 1305
source_issues.evidence: Aider crashes on startup with PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.aider/caches/versioncheck'. The app is completely unusable — main() exits before any functionality is accessible.

signals.topic: Uncaught AttributeError from litellm integration preventing app launch
signals.summary: Aider crashes on startup with AttributeError: module 'litellm' has no attribute 'APIConnectionError', blocking the entire application from running when certain litellm versions are installed.
signals.review_reason: Full application startup crash — the AttributeError occurs in LiteLLMExceptions.__init__ called from base_coder.py send_message before the user can interact with the tool. The litellm library version mismatch causes a hard crash rather than graceful degradation. The tool is completely unusable for affected users on Windows 10 with this litellm version.

source_issues.title: Uncaught AttributeError in exceptions.py line 74
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: module 'litellm' has no attribute 'APIConnectionError' thrown in exceptions.py __init__, called from send_message before the interactive loop begins. App crashes with full traceback on Windows 10.

signals.topic: Uncaught NotImplementedError on `/add` command with absolute path patterns (Windows)
signals.summary: Aider crashes with NotImplementedError when running `/add` with absolute path patterns on Windows, blocking the core file-add workflow.
signals.review_reason: While the issue was closed, the NotImplementedError in pathlib.py's glob implementation is a fundamental Windows path handling bug. The /add command — a core user workflow — crashes entirely on Windows when users use absolute paths. The underlying Python limitation means the issue likely persists for Windows users.

source_issues.title: Uncaught NotImplementedError in pathlib.py line 1090
source_issues.evidence: NotImplementedError: Non-relative patterns are unsupported thrown in pathlib.py line 1090 when Path.glob() is called on Windows. The crash occurs in commands.py cmd_add -> glob_filtered_to_repo(), blocking the fundamental file-add workflow.

signals.topic: Uncaught TypeError in analytics.py crashing app on launch
signals.summary: Aider crashes on startup due to TypeError in analytics.py caused by analytics library version incompatibility with the capture() call signature, preventing the app from starting.
signals.review_reason: App launch crash with full traceback — analytics.event('launched') in main.py line 664 throws TypeError before the user reaches the interactive loop. This is caused by an analytics library version incompatibility where the capture() API signature changed, making the tool completely unusable for users with the affected library version.

source_issues.title: Uncaught TypeError in analytics.py line 240
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Client.capture() got multiple values for argument 'distinct_id' in analytics.py line 240. The crash occurs in main() before the interactive loop, in the analytics.event('launched') call. This is a version incompatibility between the analytics library and the calling code.

signals.topic: Gitignore false positive silently blocks file edits and commits
signals.summary: After manually adding files to a session, aider incorrectly treats subsequent auto-added files as matching gitignore spec, causing edits to be skipped and commits to fail with false 'Skipping edits that matches gitignore spec' warnings.
aliases: Gitignore spec false positive after manual file add
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking bug that causes aider to wrongly skip legitimate file edits and fail commits after a manual file addition. The user must close and reopen the session to recover, which is a significant disruption. The false positive gitignore detection creates a state where the core edit-and-commit workflow is entirely blocked.

source_issues.title: browser version won't auto add files or commit changes if files are manually added
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'if I add files manually for context, it won't auto add any other files, and it won't commit the changes, saying they are part of the gitignore now. The error/warning is: Skipping edits to filename.cs that matches gitignore spec (regardless of whether it does or not). Only workaround is closing and reopening the session.' The gitignore is confirmed to be set up correctly.

signals.topic: openai:chat provider ignores apiKeyEnvar config, requiring OPENAI_API_KEY even for OpenRouter/custom API hosts
signals.summary: When using openai:chat with apiKeyEnvar (e.g., OPENROUTER_API_KEY), the provider silently ignores the config and requires OPENAI_API_KEY. The pre-flight validation bypasses getApiKey() and checks OPENAI_API_KEY directly, making the apiKeyEnvar option non-functional.
signals.review_reason: This is a real authentication/permission issue that blocks users from using openai:chat with third-party OpenAI-compatible APIs (OpenRouter, Together AI, etc.) without setting OPENAI_API_KEY. The apiKeyEnvar config option is documented but completely non-functional due to pre-flight validation bypassing getApiKey(). Workaround is awkward and not always viable.

source_issues.title: openai:chat provider ignores apiKeyEnvar config — requires OPENAI_API_KEY even for OpenRouter
source_issues.evidence: Using openai:chat with apiKeyEnvar: OPENROUTER_API_KEY still fails with 'API key is not set. Set the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable.' Pre-flight validation bypasses getApiKey() method. Workaround requires switching to openrouter: prefix which breaks custom apiHost support.

signals.topic: OpenClaw provider fails with 'missing scope: operator.write' due to missing device identity pairing
signals.summary: When using openclaw:agent:agentid provider, requests fail with 'missing scope: operator.write'. OpenClaw's newer gateway requires client connections to include a paired device identity, without which agent/session write operations fail entirely.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear authentication/permission issue that completely blocks usage of OpenClaw agents via the openclaw:agent provider. All agent/session write operations fail with a scope error. The integration gap is on the promptfoo side as it does not handle the new paired device identity requirement.

source_issues.title: Openclaw provider fails in openclaw:agent:agentid
source_issues.evidence: Connection reaches OpenClaw gateway but fails with 'missing scope: operator.write'. The root cause is that OpenClaw's newer gateway requires paired device identity which promptfoo does not provide, blocking all write operations on openclaw agents.

signals.topic: MCP scan fails when using own OPENAI_API_KEY — remote generation requirement blocks local pipeline usage
signals.summary: Running promptfoo scan in CI/CD pipelines with a self-provided OPENAI_API_KEY fails because certain test strategies (e.g., jailbreak:meta) require remote generation. Users see 'Email Verification Required' errors or 'remote generation is currently disabled' errors, preventing MCP scan from running in containerized/CI environments.
aliases: MCP scan OPENAI_API_KEY blocks red team
promptfoo scan fails in docker CI pipeline
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking issue that prevents MCP scan from running in CI/CD pipelines. Users who provide their own OPENAI_API_KEY are blocked from running red team strategies that require remote generation. This is a critical friction point for users integrating promptfoo into automated pipelines.

source_issues.title: Unable to run MCP scan - Remote generation mandated
source_issues.evidence: Users cannot run promptfoo scan in Harness pipeline inside Docker with their own OPEN AI key. Errors include 'Email Verification Required' and 'jailbreak:meta strategy requires remote generation, which is currently disabled (commonly because OPENAI_API_KEY is set)'.

signals.topic: temperature=0 handled inconsistently between openai:chat and openai:responses APIs — causes non-deterministic eval results
signals.summary: Temperature=0 in the openai:chat endpoint was fixed to produce deterministic results, but the same fix was not applied to openai:responses endpoint. Users running evals against responses endpoints get non-deterministic results even with temperature=0, breaking reproducibility of evaluation results.
signals.review_reason: This causes non-deterministic evaluation results when using the openai:responses endpoint with temperature=0, directly undermining the core reproducibility guarantee of promptfoo evals. The fix was applied to chat endpoints but not to responses endpoints, creating a silent inconsistency.

source_issues.title: temperature: 0 is handled differently between chat and responses APIs
source_issues.evidence: Both openai:chat and openai:responses configured with temperature: 0 should produce deterministic results, but only chat endpoints do. Responses endpoint has the same bugs that chat endpoints previously had. This causes non-reproducible eval scores.

signals.topic: Red team crescendo strategy LLM rubric evaluation ignores full conversation history — produces false failures
signals.summary: When running red team scan with crescendo strategy (stateful multi-turn conversation), the LLM rubric evaluation only sees the most recent message instead of the full conversation context. This causes false negative evaluations where the system is flagged for exposing information that was actually provided by the user in an earlier message of the same conversation.
aliases: red team multi-turn evaluation missing history
signals.review_reason: This causes false negative results in red team evaluations — the system is incorrectly flagged for exposing PII that was actually provided by the user themselves earlier in the conversation. This undermines the reliability of red team scan results and can lead to wasted investigation of non-issues.

source_issues.title: Red team rubric evaluation does not include all messages context using crescendo strategy
source_issues.evidence: Crescendo strategy with stateful: true produces false failures. Evaluation reports user info was exposed without being in the user's request, but the info was provided by the user in the first message of the conversation. The LLM rubric only receives the latest message, not the full history.

signals.topic: Multiple OpenAI Responses API serialization bugs cause data loss and API schema mismatches
signals.summary: Six distinct bugs in the OpenAI Responses API implementation: (1) Assistant text silently dropped when tool calls present; (2) ResponseOutputMessage.phase not preserved; (3) input_file serialized with wrong nested structure not matching OpenAI schema; (4) Reasoning model snapshot lookup too strict; (5) Reasoning token count duplicated across all ThinkingBlocks; (6) Tool call arguments inconsistently serialized as dict instead of JSON string.
aliases: Assistant text dropped with tool calls
signals.review_reason: This cluster of bugs is P0 because it affects the core OpenAI Responses API integration with GPT-5.x in multi-turn tool-calling workflows — a primary use case. Issues #21124, #21146, and #21121 all reference the same serialization path (to_openai_responses_message_dict), confirming systematic failure. Data loss (text dropped), schema mismatches (API rejection), and token counting errors directly break production RAG and agent pipelines.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Multiple bugs in llama-index-llms-openai
source_issues.evidence: Six bugs identified in multi-turn tool-calling workflow with GPT-5.x. Assistant text dropped silently, phase not preserved, reasoning tokens duplicated across blocks, tool kwargs not serialized as JSON strings.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: to_openai_responses_message_dict serializes input_file using nested 'file' object, which does not match current OpenAI Responses API schema
source_issues.evidence: DocumentBlock serialized as {type:input_file, file:{filename,file_data}} but OpenAI API expects flat {type:input_file, filename, file_data}. Causes API schema validation failures.

source_issues.title: [Feature Request]: Support DocumentBlock(url=...) serialization to OpenAI Responses input_file.file_url (instead of forcing file_data)
source_issues.evidence: Related: file_url forwarding capability needed alongside the schema fix, showing the nested structure is also causing capability gaps.

signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever async event loop blocking breaks async production workflows
signals.summary: QueryFusionRetriever._aretrieve calls synchronous _get_queries() which blocks on self._llm.complete(), preventing other coroutines on the same event loop from making progress until query expansion finishes.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed async runtime bug where synchronous LLM calls block the event loop in async production workflows. The reproduction case proves the event loop stalls — other coroutines cannot make progress during query expansion. This is a production-blocking issue for users running async retrieval pipelines (e.g., FastAPI + Uvicorn), not a theoretical concern.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `QueryFusionRetriever._aretrieve` blocks the event loop during query generation
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code shows other_work done: False when it should be True after 0.1s sleep, proving event loop is blocked. Default num_queries > 1 triggers the blocking path.

signals.topic: Google reranker fails silently in production async context while working in tests/Jupyter
signals.summary: Google RankServiceAsyncClient used in _apostprocess_nodes causes silent failures in production React agent deployments. Removing the async client and falling back to the default asyncio.to_thread wrapper makes it work.
signals.review_reason: Clear user-facing failure in production: the reranker silently fails and makes the entire query engine return an error message to end users. This is not a low-level issue — it directly breaks the main agent interaction flow in production deployments, even though the same code works in test environments.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Google reranker does not work in production
source_issues.evidence: User reports reranker works fine in tests and Jupyter notebook but fails in production React agent deployments, causing the virtual assistant to return 'technical issues with the tools' error. Root cause is async client usage in production threads.

signals.topic: DocumentBlock(url=...) uses blocking requests.get in async astream_chat path, causing 504 timeouts in production
signals.summary: In async workflows using astream_chat_with_tools, DocumentBlock with remote URLs is resolved via synchronous requests.get, which blocks the async event loop and causes HTTP 504 errors when upstream is under load.
signals.review_reason: Although labeled 'enhancement', this is a production-blocking async bug: synchronous requests.get called inside an async context blocks the event loop and causes 504 HTTP errors that fail workflow steps. The user provides explicit production stack trace and deployment context (FastAPI + Uvicorn + AWS ECS). This directly blocks the main async workflow.

source_issues.title: [Feature Request]: DocumentBlock(url=...) uses blocking `requests` in async chat path (`astream_chat`), causing timeouts in production
source_issues.evidence: User on FastAPI+Uvicorn AWS ECS/Fargate production deployment gets requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 504 when upstream is under load. Blocking requests.get in async path is confirmed root cause. Issue is labeled enhancement but the behavior is a production-blocking async bug.

signals.topic: Dependency conflict prevents upgrading Azure OpenAI LLM and embedding packages simultaneously
signals.summary: llama-index-embeddings-azure-openai 0.5.1 has a dependency constraint requiring llama-index-llms-azure-openai>=0.4.0,<0.5, which conflicts with the newer llama-index-llms-azure-openai>=0.5.0,<0.6.0. This creates an unsatisfiable dependency conflict blocking package upgrades for Azure OpenAI users.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed dependency constraint bug that prevents users from upgrading both Azure LLM and embedding packages to their latest versions. The uv package manager explicitly rejects the combination with a 'no solution found' error. This blocks Azure OpenAI users from accessing newer features and security fixes in both packages.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: llama-index-embeddings-azure-openai 0.5.1 is still dependent on llama-index-llms-azure-openai>=0.4.0,<0.5

signals.topic: CLI memory subcommands hang indefinitely after completion (ONNX worker threads keep process alive)
signals.summary: All `ruflo memory` subcommands (init, stats, store, search, list, cleanup, compress) hang indefinitely after completing their work. The root cause is that ONNX/WASM worker threads spawned by the ONNX runtime keep the Node.js event loop alive. The CLI entry point (`bin/cli.js`) only called `process.exit()` on the error path, relying on natural Node.js exit on success — which never happens due to the orphaned worker threads. Affects all memory subcommands, not just `memory init`.
aliases: CLI process does not exit after memory commands
ONNX worker threads prevent Node.js from exiting
ruflo memory subcommands hang after completion
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow-blocking bug. Users run memory commands and the process never exits, requiring manual termination. Count=2 confirms this is not an isolated incident. It blocks the core memory tool usage workflow. P1 (not P0) because count=2 and while it is blocking, it affects a specific tool category (memory) rather than the entire CLI.

source_issues.title: fix: ruflo memory subcommands hang after completion — process.exit() missing from CLI entry point
source_issues.evidence: All `ruflo memory` subcommands hang indefinitely. ONNX/WASM worker threads keep the Node.js event loop alive. CLI entry point only exits on error path, not on success. Fix requires adding `process.exit(0)` in the entry point. The original fix (issue #1428) only patched one command individually.

source_issues.title: memory init hangs after completion — process does not exit (ONNX worker threads not terminated)

The token optimization loop is a core differentiator and it silently fails on Windows — returning empty output rather than an error, so users may not realize savings are lost. Causes financial impact (no token savings) without users knowing why. P1 despite count=1 because the claim of '30-50% token savings' being completely unachievable on an entire OS platform is a significant, concrete impact.

signals.topic: streamText streaming OOM: parsePartialOutput creates O(n) string copies causing container OOM kills
signals.summary: streamText default text() output calls parsePartialOutput on every chunk, then JSON.stringify(result.partial), which forces V8 to flatten accumulated ConsStrings into full copies on each chunk. For a 110KB response in 13,000 chunks this creates ~350MB of string copies per stream. With 3 concurrent streams on a 4GB container, heap reached ~3.4GB causing OOM kills. Fix is a one-line return undefined from parsePartialOutput for plain text.
signals.review_reason: Directly causes production OOM kills on containers. Multiple concurrent streams compound memory usage, reaching 3.4GB on a 4GB container. Verified by heap snapshots and production deployment with before/after measurements. This is a main-flow failure (streaming) with severe cost impact (container restarts).

source_issues.title: streamText Memory Issue: parsePartialOutput creates O(n) string copies
source_issues.evidence: Heap snapshot shows 14,351 string copies totaling 1.6GB. Before fix: 3374MB heap, 95% container memory. After fix: 133MB heap, 10% container memory. Production containers with 4GB limit were OOM killed by this issue. Multiple concurrent streams compound the problem multiplicatively.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/xai responses stream drops final text fragments in doStream when content block already exists

signals.topic: Async stack trace degradation: async () => promiseReturningFunction pattern loses call site in error traces
signals.summary: Throughout the SDK, the pattern async (...) => promiseReturningFunction(...) (without await) is used at public abstraction boundaries. This causes async stack traces to omit or degrade the call site, especially across layered wrappers and streaming/telemetry boundaries. This makes debugging production errors extremely difficult. The fix is to use return await at public boundaries.
aliases: debugging experience degraded by async wrapper pattern
signals.review_reason: Production debugging is severely impaired. Error traces lack user call site, making it extremely difficult to identify which request or model caused a failure. This directly impacts developer productivity and makes it hard to diagnose API errors in production.

source_issues.title: Horrific debugging experience, due to misuse of async (...) => promiseReturningFunction(...)

The error message shows a 400 from llama.cpp but the trace stops deep in provider-utils without revealing which model or request triggered the failure. User had to manually patch async to await to get any useful stack information.

signals.topic: Documentation gap: 'use cache' directive silently fails in serverless environments
